_comment: Copy this machine-local file beside roster.json (`triage.py init` does it), then adapt it: drop the ecosystems you do not use, add your own paths. Every name and path under me / gerrit / clones / gateways / order is an example value.

Glob semantics: ** matches any characters including /; * and ? do not cross /; a pattern without / matches the basename only. `**/tests/**` needs a directory before tests/, so top-level paths get their own `tests/**` rule.

risk_default MEDIUM: any change gets two review legs unless you lower it. delta_triggers only RAISE, here to HIGH, for part of dev-lead SKILL.md's HIGH list: auth/security/crypto, migration, billing/payments and notifications paths (path alone), and added lines that look like a credential, a concurrency primitive, a destructive command, a CI write permission or secret, or a root/piped-installer container. They are examples for the file kinds named in each rule: extend them to your languages, and add your own partial-failure paths (retries, queues, offline sync). Lower risk_default to LOW only once your triggers raise every behaviour-changing path.

Each trigger takes one glob, so a rule for several file kinds is repeated per glob. Never give a trigger a glob that matches every file (** or *): unmatched_files counts trigger globs as coverage, so it would hide every gap.
lenses map file kinds to review lenses (the brief each leg gets); a file no lens or trigger covers is listed in unmatched_files -- a gap worth a rule.
gerrit, clones and gateways are read only by `change`; a file used for `scope` alone may leave them out.

small_delta_lines also sizes a fix round of your own change (`scope --fix-of <reviewed head>`): a fix within it, with --fix-tested evidence, takes one leg. An optional wording_globs list replaces the default that makes a fix wording only, no leg: the suffixes .md .markdown .rst .adoc, except agent instruction files (AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md GEMINI.md QUANTA.md SKILL.md).
